programs.nl_rule:
The input grid contains one or more rectangles outlined entirely in red (R) cells. Each rectangle's border is a complete, axis-aligned loop of R cells. The interior of each rectangle (the cells enclosed by the red border) is filled with black (.) cells except for exactly one red (R) cell somewhere inside, which serves as a marker. The rest of the grid outside the rectangles is black (.) background.

For each red-bordered rectangle in the grid: (1) Measure the interior dimensions — that is, the width and height of the space enclosed by the red border, not counting the border itself. (2) Based on the interior size, choose a fill color: 3×3 interior → azure (A), 5×5 interior → yellow (Y), 7×7 interior → green (G). (3) Replace every black (.) cell inside the rectangle's border with the chosen fill color. (4) Leave the single red (R) marker cell inside the rectangle unchanged. (5) Leave the red border itself and all cells outside rectangles unchanged.

The grid dimensions match the input exactly. The background is black (.). All rectangles have square interiors with odd side lengths (3, 5, or 7). Red (R) cells form the borders and interior markers and remain unchanged in the output. The only change is that interior black cells become azure, yellow, or green depending on the rectangle's interior size.
